Sokoto State Governor, Ahmed Aliyu, has announced plans to construct the road linking the Trade Fair Complex to Pinnacle Hotel, as his administration intensifies efforts to expand urban infrastructure and improve economic activities in the state capital. The governor made the announcement on Sunday while commissioning the Offa Road project in Sokoto metropolis, describing the new construction plan as part of his administration’s commitment to opening up communities and improving connectivity across the state. Aliyu said the proposed road would further enhance the socio-economic wellbeing of residents, particularly those living and conducting businesses around the area. “Let me announce that this administration is set to construct the Trade Fair Complex to Pinnacle Hotel road in our continued efforts to enhance the socio-economic wellbeing of people living in this part of the state,” he said. The governor explained that the newly commissioned Offa Road was also part of his administration’s urban renewal programme designed to transform Sokoto metropolis through improved road networks. He disclosed that his administration had completed and commissioned more than 100 township roads across the state since assuming office, while several others were at various stages of completion. Beyond its infrastructure significance, the governor said the Offa Road project represented the fulfilment of a campaign promise made to residents before the 2023 governorship election. He noted that although the community did not vote for him, his administration proceeded with the project because governance should not be influenced by political affiliations. “Although this community did not vote for us in that election, we nevertheless resolved to fulfil that promise because governance is not about political affiliations or voting patterns. Rather, it is about serving the people and providing infrastructure that improves their lives,” he said. He also cited the construction of the Sahara area road network, which he said was completed within the first 100 days of his administration, as another demonstration of his commitment to delivering infrastructure without discrimination. Describing roads as essential to economic development, Aliyu said the Offa Road would ease transportation, improve access to residential areas and business centres, facilitate the movement of goods and services and stimulate commercial activities. He added that improved road infrastructure would also enhance access to educational institutions and healthcare facilities while contributing to security and environmental improvement. The governor commended the Ministry of Lands and Housing, contractors, consultants, engineers and other stakeholders for their contributions to the successful execution of the project. He appealed to residents and motorists to protect the road against abuse, stressing that maintaining public infrastructure was a shared responsibility. Aliyu assured the people that his administration would continue to prioritise projects capable of improving living standards, expanding economic opportunities and promoting sustainable urban and rural development. He also commended President Bola Tinubu for what he described as ongoing infrastructural transformation across the country. The latest announcement signals a continuation of the state government’s urban renewal drive, with more road projects expected to improve connectivity and support economic activities across Sokoto metropolis.
